shipped_rows.title_o: When processing costs impact predictive processing: The case of foreign-accented speech and accent experience
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: We demonstrate our approach by carrying out a single change replication of an in-person eye-tracking study by Porretta et al. [...] Our main models show that predictive sentence processing is modulated by restrictive and non-restrictive verb type in line with Porretta et al. (2020) and that accented speech impedes predictive processing but does not preclude it. Interestingly, our accent models did not find evidence of accent-experience modulating predictive processing.

parent_scope_objection: Final second and last review, preserving initial call. Independent source validator and parent read the primary source and raised these specific unresolved scientific questions. Address each from actual source: Scope objection: the source states Porretta’s two research questions but never states what its accent-experience analysis found. The new main models are expressly in line with Porretta; the new accent models are null and called inconclusive, with lower exposure, power and measurement issues discussed. A research question is not an original finding, so the implicit-comparison requirement (original result and corresponding new result) is unmet for the purported failed accent effect. The expert addresses uncertainty by repeating the questions and new null, not by supplying the missing original result. Mixed therefore needs further justification; the supported main-model comparison must be kept separate from an unestablished accent contrast.
